findings.passage: If either documents a habit of embellishing his story, an argument built on self-report weakens and Type 3 gains.
findings.problem: The page treats as a hypothetical something three openable sources already report. Reviews of Mike Wilson's 1997 biography, opened on 2026-11-12, say what the book documents. Kirkus: he 'seems to specialize in reinventing himself. By all accounts, he grew up on middle-class South Shore Drive, but he has told reporters that he lived in the South Side ghetto', and he would 'imply he had an advanced degree in physics'. Publishers Weekly: Wilson 'does a solid job of punching holes in the myths', including that he 'didn't grow up on the streets of Chicago, as he has led some to believe, nor does he have a college degree, let alone the graduate degrees attributed to him'. Computergram (October 20, 1997) relays a childhood friend's account that he 'made up delightful and often plausible details', stories that 'glorified Larry Ellison', and an ex-employee's 'Larry always had a problem with tenses'. By the article's own sentence this weakens an argument built on self-report and helps Type 3, and invented self-flattering stories are image evidence in their own right. The Type 8 lead currently rests on four self-reports. The record (type_hypothesis.against, C47, C58) does not weigh any of this, and research task 1 calls it 'expected by a reviewer from memory, not verified'.
findings.acceptance_test: The three reviews (kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/mike-wilson/the-difference-between-god-and-larry-ellison, publishersweekly.com/9780688149253, techmonitor.ai/?p=186352), or the book itself, are opened and added as sources. The conditional sentence is replaced by a plain, attributed statement of what reviewers say Wilson documents, worded as their report of the book and not as the profile's own finding. The Why-not-Type-3 section counts it for Type 3, and type_hypothesis.against and a new claim carry it. The text then says in one or two sentences why Type 8 still leads at medium confidence with that evidence weighed, or lowers the confidence, or changes the lead. If the lead type changes, hold for --refresh --expanded-review. The 60-word answer, FAQs 1 and 2 and the description match the result. The body stays at or under 4,500 words by the contract counter: cut before adding.

findings.passage: Mike Wilson's unauthorized _The Difference Between God and Larry Ellison_ (1997)
findings.problem: No opened source calls the book unauthorized, and two opened reviews point the other way: Kirkus calls it 'An authorized biography' and Publishers Weekly says Ellison 'agreed to be interviewed for the book'. The source note for S33 repeats 'unauthorized'.
findings.acceptance_test: 'Unauthorized' is removed from the body and the S33 note, or replaced with what an opened source supports (for example, that Ellison gave Wilson interviews).

findings.passage: The Hurd email was a shot at a competitor's board.
findings.problem: The edit introduced this sentence. The cited Reuters report (S14) says 'Oracle ... is a major partner of HP' and 'now also competes with HP in the server market'. Calling HP only a competitor makes the calculating reading look cleaner than the source allows; attacking a major partner's board carried commercial risk.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence says HP was both a major partner and, since the Sun purchase, a competitor, or drops the characterisation.

findings.passage: It is also the failing he named in 2002, after three marriages: "I shouldn't seek to control her anymore than I would want her to control me."
findings.problem: The quotation is exact, but the two sentences before it in S03 say what kind of control he meant: 'I had an irrational standard of behavior for myself. If she didn't conform to the same standard, I would become annoyed.' That is holding a partner to his own standard. It is one of the four self-reports the Type 8 case counts, and the omitted lines read at least as much like a One or a Three as an Eight.
findings.acceptance_test: The passage quotes or accurately paraphrases the 'irrational standard of behavior for myself' sentences, and the text does not present the marriage remark as evidence of an Eight's control without that context.

findings.passage: In 1997 he named the core of his personality as "questioning conventional wisdom, doubting the experts, and questioning authority."
findings.problem: His words in S02 are narrower: 'The most important aspect of my personality, as far as determining my success goes, has been my questioning conventional wisdom...' He is naming the trait that explains his success. A related overreach opens the surveillance section, 'Ellison says the authority he first questioned was his father's faith in the state'; he says his father never questioned the government and did not want him to question authority, and names teachers alongside him.
findings.acceptance_test: Both lead-ins claim no more than the 1997 text: the trait he credits for his success, and a father who never questioned the government and did not want him to question authority.

findings.passage: An Eight's need for control explains how a workplace, a marriage or a sales culture ends up arranged around one man's judgment.
